key_insight: Tabular foundation models are strong on small to medium IID benchmarks, but their advantage drops on harder non-IID, large, and high-dimensional datasets.
engineering_relevance: For real-world tabular ML systems, benchmark choice matters: performance claims should be validated on temporal, grouped, and high-dimensional data, not just standard IID tests.
method: Introduced BeyondArena, a unified benchmark spanning IID, temporal, and grouped tabular tasks.
Created Data Foundry, a Python framework plus metadata schema for curating tabular predictive datasets.
Evaluated 11 models on 142 curated datasets across varied sample sizes, feature types, and disciplines.
evidence_signal: Across 142 curated datasets, the abstract reports that tabular foundation models lead on tiny-to-medium IID data, while tree-based and deep learning methods remain stronger on non-IID, large, and high-dimensional settings.
watch_item: Benchmark results may still depend on dataset curation quality and coverage, so broad claims about generality should be tested beyond the curated benchmark set.
paper_title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?
